segments.title: Why historians seek out physical history
segments.summary: Historians visit places and objects because seeing and touching material evidence creates a different understanding from reading about it.
segments.body: Historians visit places and surviving objects because physical encounters can produce a different understanding from reading alone. The Ship Shape crew's trips to Japan and Scandinavia are examples of this kind of historical travel. Seeing and touching material evidence makes the past tangible in ways that a written description cannot fully reproduce. In-person observation adds a sense of scale, texture, and presence that remains abstract on the page.
segments.question: Why do historians like to visit historical places and objects in person?
segments.answerShort: Because seeing and touching physical evidence can provide an understanding that reading alone cannot supply.

evidence.note: He contrasts physical encounter with reading and says it produces a different understanding.

segments.title: HMS Warspite's surviving barbette steel
segments.summary: A curved, heavy fragment of HMS Warspite's barbette steel gives a direct sense of the battleship's construction and scale.
segments.body: A surviving piece of HMS Warspite's barbette steel gives a direct sense of the battleship's physical scale. Its curvature, thickness, and weight make the protected gun position easier to grasp than specifications or photographs alone. The fragment is one of the last remaining chunks of the ship, yet it sits in a local DIY store's car park rather than in a museum. Its unusual setting adds to the emotional force of seeing and touching part of the famous warship. The piece preserves evidence of Warspite's materials and scale even though most of the ship is gone.

evidence.note: He identifies the fragment as HMS Warspite barbette steel and discusses its curvature, thickness, weight, and rarity.
He describes the fragment's emotional force, its unusual car-park setting, and why physical history matters especially for naval historians.
